title: Bahai Badi Calendar
intro: The Badí' calendar is used in the Bahá'í Faith. Its year has nineteen months of nineteen days each, with a short group of intercalary days and a New Year associated with the spring equinox.
summary: Nineteen months of nineteen days, plus four or five extra days.
epoch: The Bahá'í Era (B.E.) begins in 1844, linked to the declaration of the Báb. Naw-Rúz marks the new year around the northern spring equinox.
epoch_heading: THE BAHÁ'Í ERA AND NEW YEAR
year_rule: Nineteen months each contain nineteen days (361 days). Ayyám-i-Há adds four or five days between the eighteenth and nineteenth months to keep the solar year aligned. In Bahá'í practice a day begins at sunset.
after_note: The Ayyám-i-Há intercalary days come before the final month, 'Alá'. Month names above use simple Roman-letter spellings; transliterations vary.
history: The Báb introduced the Badí' calendar and Bahá'u'lláh confirmed it. Its months take names from attributes of God. The worldwide Bahá'í system fixes Naw-Rúz by the equinox and observes dates from sunset to sunset; this software's earlier dates and distant-year continuation follow its documented computational model.
limits: This provider uses a fixed 21 March rule for Bahá'í years 1-171, a Tehran equinox/sunset model from year 172 within its validated range, and an extrapolation outside that range. It does not certify all historical observances or distant astronomical predictions.
